title: Mister B and Angle in Polygon
statementMd:
On one quiet day all of sudden Mister B decided to draw angle $*a*$ on his field. Aliens have already visited his field and left many different geometric figures on it. One of the figures is **regular convex $*n*$-gon** (regular convex polygon with $*n*$ sides).

That's why Mister B decided to use this polygon. Now Mister B must find three distinct vertices $*v*_{1}$, $*v*_{2}$, $*v*_{3}$ such that the angle ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c96cdfe08c576797192f794d1c8f9c5948471c4e.png) (where $*v*_{2}$ is the vertex of the angle, and $*v*_{1}$ and $*v*_{3}$ lie on its sides) is as close as possible to $*a*$. In other words, the value ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a065e60ada2155058fd60edbc54771fbad586d48.png) should be minimum possible.

If there are many optimal solutions, Mister B should be satisfied with any of them.

## Input

First and only line contains two space-separated integers $*n*$ and $*a*$ ($3 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $1 ≤ *a* ≤ 180$) — the number of vertices in the polygon and the needed angle, in degrees.

## Output

Print three space-separated integers: the vertices $*v*_{1}$, $*v*_{2}$, $*v*_{3}$, which form ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c96cdfe08c576797192f794d1c8f9c5948471c4e.png). If there are multiple optimal solutions, print any of them. The vertices are numbered from $1$ to $*n*$ in clockwise order.

## Note

In first sample test vertices of regular triangle can create only angle of $60$ degrees, that's why every possible angle is correct.

Vertices of square can create $45$ or $90$ degrees angles only. That's why in second sample test the angle of $45$ degrees was chosen, since $|45 - 67| < |90 - 67|$. Other correct answers are: "3 1 2", "3 2 4", "4 2 3", "4 3 1", "1 3 4", "1 4 2", "2 4 1", "4 1 3", "3 1 4", "3 4 2", "2 4 3", "2 3 1", "1 3 2", "1 2 4", "4 2 1".

In third sample test, on the contrary, the angle of $90$ degrees was chosen, since $|90 - 68| < |45 - 68|$. Other correct answers are: "2 1 4", "3 2 1", "1 2 3", "4 3 2", "2 3 4", "1 4 3", "3 4 1".
statementZhMd:
<statement>
在一个宁静的日子里，B先生突然决定在自己的田地上画出角 $*a*$。此前，外星人来过他的田地，并在上面留下了许多不同的几何图形。其中一个图形是**正凸 $*n*$ 边形**（具有 $*n*$ 条边的正凸多边形）。

因此，B先生决定使用这个多边形。现在，他必须找出三个互不相同的顶点 $*v*_{1}$、$*v*_{2}$、$*v*_{3}$，使角 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c96cdfe08c576797192f794d1c8f9c5948471c4e.png)（其中 $*v*_{2}$ 是角的顶点，$*v*_{1}$ 和 $*v*_{3}$ 位于角的两条边上）与 $*a*$ 尽可能接近。换句话说，数值 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a065e60ada2155058fd60edbc54771fbad586d48.png) 应当尽可能小。

如果有多个最优解，B先生可以接受其中任意一个。

## 输入格式

唯一一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$ 和 $*a*$（$3 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$1 ≤ *a* ≤ 180$），分别表示多边形的顶点数和所需的角度，单位为度。

## 输出格式

输出三个用空格分隔的整数：顶点 $*v*_{1}$、$*v*_{2}$、$*v*_{3}$，它们构成角 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c96cdfe08c576797192f794d1c8f9c5948471c4e.png)。如果有多个最优解，输出其中任意一个。顶点按照顺时针顺序编号为 $1$ 至 $*n*$。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，正三角形的顶点只能构成 $60$ 度的角，因此任意一个可能的角都是正确的。

正方形的顶点只能构成 $45$ 度或 $90$ 度的角。因此在第二个样例中选择了 $45$ 度的角，因为 $|45 - 67| < |90 - 67|$。其他正确答案包括："3 1 2"、"3 2 4"、"4 2 3"、"4 3 1"、"1 3 4"、"1 4 2"、"2 4 1"、"4 1 3"、"3 1 4"、"3 4 2"、"2 4 3"、"2 3 1"、"1 3 2"、"1 2 4"、"4 2 1"。

在第三个样例中则相反，选择了 $90$ 度的角，因为 $|90 - 68| < |45 - 68|$。其他正确答案包括："2 1 4"、"3 2 1"、"1 2 3"、"4 3 2"、"2 3 4"、"1 4 3"、"3 4 1"。
</statement>
